title: Reverse Geocoder: Coordinates to Address Fields
description: Turn coordinates into address fields with the Reverse Geocoder — road, city, region, postcode and country for any point. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, clicking a point in the middle of Chicago returns the full stack — road, city, county-grade region, postcode 60601, country — the complete sentence that two bare numbers were abbreviating.
quick_answer: The Reverse Geocoder takes coordinates you paste or a point you click and returns its address fields — road, city, region, postcode and country. It is the mirror of geocoding: numbers in, the place's written address out, field by field, ready to copy into whatever asked for it.

A spreadsheet of coordinates gains city and postcode columns one careful paste at a time — with the batch route noted for hundreds.
A point claims to be at an address; the reverse read checks whether the record agrees. Disagreements find swapped digits fast.
What does a reverse geocoder actually return at this point? This page is the honest specimen before you build on any API.
The result is structured — road, city, region, postcode, country as separate fields — because addresses are data, and data should travel in pieces, not paragraphs.
A desert or ocean point returns few fields or none. The emptiness is the information, and this page shows it plainly instead of borrowing the nearest town's name.

faq: A public reverse geocoder over OpenStreetMap data — the same open stack as this site's other address tools, with results shown field by field.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — paste or click any coordinates; your own position is never the input.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Different geocoders hold different records and vintages; the same point can return a neighbouring road or an older postcode elsewhere.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
That is batch work — the Batch Geocoder handles lists; this page is the careful single-point instrument.
Is the road the point's address?
It is the nearest recorded road — a point inside a large property may sit nearer another road than its postal one. Address-grade certainty belongs to postal authorities.
Expect emptiness or a sea name — the honest answer for water, as the Ocean or Land Checker formalises.
Precision of the point versus the fields?
Your input can be metre-precise while fields stay street-level: records describe places, not survey marks.
Yes — fields are presented separately precisely so each can be copied alone.
